page: Vultr vhp-1c-2gb-intel is an entry-level virtual machine within the High Performance family, configured with 1 shared Intel Xeon vCPU clocked at 2.0 GHz, 2.0 GB of system memory, and 50 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage. The x86_64 processor architecture includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 4 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX, AVX-512F, AVX-512 VNNI, and AES-NI hardware cryptography, though the CPU allocation relies on a single shared physical thread without hyper-threading.

Benchmark results reflect the single-threaded shared resource profile of the instance. The stress-ng single-core test reaches 1421.58, placing it in the middle 50% relative performance band. However, overall multi-core and throughput evaluations land in the lower percentiles due to the single-core limitation. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth is measured at 7.43 GB/sec with write throughput at 6.32 GB/sec. Application-level metrics show 1.62 million Redis SET operations per second and 1.85 GB/sec static web serving throughput.

From a cost efficiency standpoint, this server provides accessible compute with high-speed local NVMe storage and an included public IPv4 address on an economical budget footprint. The main performance bottleneck is the shared single-core CPU and limited 2 GB memory ceiling, which restrict concurrent task handling and memory-heavy workloads.
This server type is suitable for microservices, lightweight development environments, low-traffic web hosting, basic automation scripts, and small utility databases.
description: Vultr vhp-1c-2gb-intel is an entry-level cloud instance from the High Performance lineup featuring 1 shared Intel Xeon vCPU operating at 2.0 GHz, 2.0 GB of RAM, and 50 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage. Built on x86_64 architecture with support for AVX-512 vector instructions and AES cryptography, its compute capacity is constrained to a single execution thread. Synthetic tests record a stress-ng single-core score of 1421.58 and static web delivery at 1.85 GB/sec, reflecting moderate single-thread execution alongside entry-level multi-core and memory subsystem metrics. Memory throughput peaks at 7.43 GB/sec for uncached reads. The combination of NVMe storage and low resource density makes it a cost-efficient platform for light utility workloads, edge proxies, microservices, and small test environments that do not experience sustained compute saturation.
